correctness.rationale: For all \(n\ge1\) every proper colouring gives rowwise injections and a loop-free indegree/outdegree≤1 colour-identification digraph. Distinct repeated colours sharing a column give exactly a bichromatic four-edge path or four-cycle, and every forbidden pattern yields two such links. Therefore feasible colourings correspond bijectively to oriented partial matchings of the n columns; k links consume \(2n-k\) unique colours and are counted by \(n!/(k!(n-2k)!)\). Named-colour choices are falling factorials; the exponential formula follows. Exact definition-based canonical partition enumeration for \(2\le n\le7\) tested 71,350 proper candidates and agreed at every coefficient. The finite test is not used to establish the infinite theorem.

value.rationale: The 2019 exact star chromatic index gives only the minimum palette. The new structural bijection and all-colour enumerator determine the complete solution distribution, all optimal-solution multiplicities, and a natural log-concavity property. Star edge-colouring and its line-graph vertex counterpart are established graph-colouring problems, so this complete infinite-family classification is mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary slice. Counting the number of optimal solutions matters for enumeration and probabilistic sampling of star colourings.
